w:r.w:t: The Agentic AI SDR is an autonomous multi-agent software system that performs the complete top-of-funnel sales workflow — from company research through to meeting booking — without continuous human involvement. A human provides a list of target companies; the system does everything else.

A Sales Development Representative (SDR) spends the majority of their working day on four activities that are repetitive, time-consuming, and do not require human judgment: researching companies, finding decision-maker contact details, writing personalised outreach emails, and managing follow-up sequences. Studies consistently show that SDRs spend less than 30% of their time actually talking to prospects — the rest is grunt work.
This is the problem the system solves.
Given a CSV file containing company names, the system autonomously:
Researches each company — website, recent news, industry, inferred pain points
Finds the right decision-maker and their verified email address
Writes a personalised cold email tailored to that specific company
Monitors for replies, classifies intent (interested / not interested / needs follow-up)
Sends a follow-up if there is no reply after 3 days
Drafts a meeting booking email when intent is classified as positive
The human only needs to appear when a meeting is ready to be confirmed. Every step before that is autonomous.

Prompts are treated as system components, not ad hoc text. Each agent that calls the Claude API has a versioned, documented prompt with a defined output schema. Changes to prompts require a version increment.

You are a business intelligence analyst. Given the content of a company website and recent news articles, produce a structured JSON summary. Be factual — only include information that is clearly supported by the provided content. Do not invent details. If information is unavailable, use null.
Prompt explicitly instructs: only use information from the provided content
Output validated — if pain_points array is empty, confidence_score must be below 0.70
Any proper noun in the output is cross-checked against the input text before dispatch

You are a sales copywriter. Write a cold outreach email from the perspective of a sales representative. The email must: (1) be under 200 words, (2) reference one specific fact about the recipient's company from the research data provided, (3) include a single clear call to action, (4) end with "To opt out, reply STOP." Do not mention pricing
. Do not claim the email is from a human if it was generated by AI.
(At what point do we reveal that it was generated by AI, if necessary at all?)

You are an email intent classifier for a B2B sales system. Classify the following email reply into exactly one of: INTERESTED, NOT_INTERESTED, NEEDS_FOLLOW_UP. Provide a confidence score between 0.0 and 1.0. INTERESTED means the person wants to continue the conversation or book a meeting. NOT_INTERESTED means explicit decline or unsubscribe. NEEDS_FOLLOW_UP means anything else — ambiguous, out of office, or a question that requires a human answer.

Before any email is sent, Agent A4 checks the leads table for an existing gmail_message_id for that lead.
If one exists, the send is blocked regardless of the current workflow status.
This prevents duplicate sends caused by orchestrator retries or system restarts.

If the system restarts mid-run (e.g. demo server restart), the orchestrator reads all lead records on startup and resumes any lead that is in a non-terminal, non-human-review state. Because all state is persisted in Supabase after every step, no work is lost.

Every decision the system makes autonomously is governed by a confidence threshold. Below the threshold, the system stops and hands control to a human. This is not a limitation — it is a feature that makes the system trustworthy in an enterprise context.
When any lead enters HUMAN_REVIEW status, the dashboard presents the human with the following context and options:
Full lead data (company, contact, all previous actions)
The AI's output that triggered escalation (e.g. raw research, classified intent)
The AI's reasoning (confidence score and brief explanation)
Predefined action buttons: Approve and Continue / Edit and Continue / Mark Closed / Skip
The human's choice is logged with a timestamp and their user ID for audit purposes.

Cold email outreach is regulated in most jurisdictions. The system is designed to be compliant with CAN-SPAM (US), GDPR (EU), and CASL (Canada) at demo scale. Full compliance for a production deployment would require additional legal review.

This section defines where the system stops and the human begins. An agentic system without defined autonomy limits is not a product — it is a liability.
18.1 What the System May Do Autonomously
Research any company in the uploaded lead list using public web sources
Look up business contact information using Hunter.io and Apollo.io
Draft personalised cold outreach emails using the Claude API
Send outbound emails from the configured Gmail account
Send one follow-up email per lead if there is no reply after 72 hours
Classify inbound reply intent when confidence score is >= 0.80
Mark a lead as CLOSED_LOST when NOT_INTERESTED classification confidence is >= 0.85
Draft a meeting booking email when INTERESTED classification confidence is >= 0.80
18.2 What Requires Human Approval Before Action
Sending any email when human_approval_required = true (set by low-confidence draft generation)
Responding to any reply where confidence score is < 0.75
Any reply that contains the words: pricing, contract, security, legal, GDPR, compliance, or enterprise
Any reply that asks whether the outreach is AI-generated
Booking a meeting — the system drafts the email but the human sends it
Marking a lead as CLOSED_LOST when confidence is between 0.75 and 0.85
18.3 What the System Will Never Do
Send more than one follow-up per lead (hard-coded maximum)
Send an email to an unverified address
Send an email to the same address more than once in a 7-day window
Claim to be a human in any email or reply
Continue processing a lead if the recipient has replied STOP or similar opt-out language
Access any data outside the leads table for a given workflow run
All autonomous actions must be observable, reversible where possible, and attributable to the specific agent and prompt version that produced them.

This section is intentionally written for a Salesforce audience — judges, mentors, or recruiters evaluating the project.

Salesforce's core product is a CRM that manages the sales pipeline. The biggest friction point in that pipeline is the top of the funnel — getting qualified leads into the system in the first place. This is exactly the problem the Agentic AI SDR solves.

Every company that uses Salesforce Sales Cloud employs SDRs. Every SDR spends the majority of their time on tasks that are rule-based, repetitive, and do not require human judgment. This system automates those tasks.

Salesforce's biggest strategic bet right now is Agentforce — their platform for deploying autonomous AI agents across the enterprise. The architecture we have built is philosophically identical to what Agentforce enables: state-managed, multi-step, autonomous workflows with defined human escalation points.
This project is a working proof of concept of the Agentforce vision, built independently and from first principles. That is the story worth telling.
20.3 What This Project Demonstrates to Salesforce Engineers
We understand agentic system design — not just LLM prompting
We designed for failure, not just the happy path
We defined autonomy limits — which is enterprise-grade thinking
We built with cost awareness and operational constraints in mind
We can scope, architect, and ship a complex system in 8 weeks

The pitch is not 'we built a chatbot that sends emails.' The pitch is: 'We built an autonomous multi-agent workflow system that executes an entire enterprise sales function — and we defined exactly where it stops and the human begins. That is what responsible agentic AI looks like.'
